evals.prompt:
Port this React component to SwiftUI for our macOS app, pixel-perfect:
{label}
evals.expected_output: SwiftUI view using strokeBorder inside the border box, padding 12+1, fixed height 32, fixedSize custom font, kerning -0.13, CSS half-leading, compositingGroup before opacity for disabled.
assertions: Draws the border inside the box with strokeBorder
Accounts for the 1 px border in padding (12 + 1)
Uses a fixed-size custom font (no text-style tracking)
Fades the disabled control as a group (compositingGroup)

evals.prompt: We have a Next.js prototype of a meeting summary: a long paragraph with inline person mention chips (avatar + name in a capsule) and a word-by-word fade-in. Rebuild it natively in SwiftUI so it looks the same and scrolls smoothly.
evals.expected_output: One Text per paragraph, chips drawn behind invisible name runs via Text.LayoutKey, TextRenderer for per-word reveal, no view per word; parity check via screenshots and pixdiff.
assertions: Renders the paragraph as one Text, not a view per word
Animates per-word reveal with a TextRenderer
Draws the chip behind the text at the run rects

evals.prompt: the settings screen I ported from tailwind looks almost right but every control is a bit bigger and the section separators sit on top of the padding, also the shadow of the floating pill is too dark. help me match the web exactly
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses stroke vs strokeBorder, border-t occupying its own row, negative-spread shadow as blurred shrunk shape; fixes in the kit; verifies with headless reference screenshot and pixdiff --ink.
assertions: Diagnoses stroke vs strokeBorder (border outside the box)
Separators occupy their own pixel row, not drawn over padding
Reproduces a negative-spread shadow by blurring a shrunk shape
Fixes in shared kit components, not per screen
Verifies with a reference screenshot and diff
